findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
findings.body: When optimized_pagination=true and the caller is a superuser or has global access, this endpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime". That class's get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on the raw attribute, and value_from_cursor returns the cursor integer unchanged. Audit log datetime values are datetimes, so the first page that returns rows raises TypeError in get_item_key, and any later page compares a datetime column to an integer. DateTimePaginator exists for this field. Org owners/managers who pass the new query flag get HTTP 500s on an otherwise working endpoint, and there is no test covering the new branch.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are passed into queryset slices
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator, when enable_advanced_features is set, slices the queryset with a client-supplied negative cursor.offset (Cursor.from_string accepts it). Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError for any negative start/stop, so this path 500s instead of paginating. The same change in BasePaginator.get_result (line 182) stops clamping offsets for previous-page cursors on every cursor paginator, not just this class. Comments claiming the ORM safely handles negative slices and that this reaches rows beyond normal bounds are wrong; it only breaks pagination or, if a backend ever accepted the slice, would turn an untrusted cursor into an unbounded offset.

findings.title: Sorted-set commands are incompatible with existing span-buffer sets
findings.body: add-buffer.lua and SpansBuffer switched segment storage from Redis sets (SADD/SCARD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN/ZPOPMIN) with no migration. Keys already written as sets remain until redis_ttl (default 3600s). The next ZADD or ZCARD against those keys returns WRONGTYPE, so process_spans fails, segments are not merged or flushed, and in-flight span data is stuck or dropped for up to an hour after deploy.

findings.title: Eviction cap is hardcoded and the Python size guard was removed
findings.body: After a merge, the script ZPOPMINs the segment down to a hardcoded 1000 members, using the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores, with no metric. SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans is 1001 and is no longer consulted: _load_segment_data dropped the check that skipped segments over that count. Caps can diverge, eviction is invisible, and any path that does not hit this Lua branch (or a WRONGTYPE failure) can now flush an unbounded segment that the old guard would have dropped.

findings.title: Redirect walk limit cut from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The parent-redirect loop now stops at 1000 hops and the comment that this limit can fail to join deep segment trees was removed. Traces whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 are no longer merged into one segment; spans stay on separate keys and are flushed as split or parentless segments. That is a silent correctness regression versus the previous script.

findings.title: Missing end_timestamp_precise crashes the span batch
findings.body: process_batch now requires val["end_timestamp_precise"] and stores it as the sorted-set score. The previous consumer did not read this field (tests had to be updated to add it). A span event that omits it raises KeyError inside the batch, which fails the whole batch and stalls the consumer instead of buffering the span. Use a safe default or skip/metric the span if the schema field is optional.

findings.title: No test for sorted-set eviction or over-limit segments
findings.body: The insert path now scores members by end_timestamp_precise and the Lua script drops members once a segment exceeds 1000 spans, and the flush-time span-count skip was deleted. Existing buffer tests only use four or five spans with identical timestamps, so they never exercise ZPOPMIN, score ordering, the 1000 cap, or a segment that used to be rejected for max_segment_spans. A wrong eviction count or a failure to trim would ship without a failing test.
